summary: A mismatch can occur at the final normalized pair examined, so palindrome recognition requires inspecting all n characters in the worst case. The two-pointer scan visits each position at most once.

optimality.argument: On a normalized palindrome, a correct algorithm must rule out a mismatch at every mirrored position; changing an unread alphanumeric character can make the string non-palindromic while preserving all inspected characters. Thus the worst-case lower bound is Omega(n). The current pointers move only inward and cross the input at most once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unread mirrored position can contain the only mismatch, so a correct worst-case palindrome decision must inspect the complete normalized content.
Each pointer advances monotonically, and no raw string position is revisited by the same pointer.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover ignored punctuation and case, a mismatch, and normalization to empty; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
